headline: High: open-webui’s broad network/MCP/file access can amplify prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors when paired with a local game agent that lacks isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui can ingest files, MCP, and web content, so attacker-controlled text can reach its prompts; godot_rl_agents is a game-playing repo with no documented isolation or parsing defenses. The pair lacks a proven shared channel, but open-webui’s default tool surfaces make injection plausible if outputs are bridged into it.
conditions: IF outputs from godot_rl_agents are copied into open-webui chats or MCP tools
IF open-webui is configured to ingest local files or web pages as instructions
mitigations: Disable MCP and file-ingest tools in open-webui
Use a separate workspace for the game agent and the web UI
Add a manual review step before pasting any agent output
Restrict open-webui to trusted sources only
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui explicitly touches files, documents, notes, persistent memory, and API keys, and has broad egress; godot_rl_agents is open-source but its profile shows no data classes touched. The pairwise leakage risk is driven by open-webui’s default data handling, especially if the game agent’s outputs or local files are imported into it.
conditions: IF godot_rl_agents outputs are stored in open-webui persistent memory or files
IF open-webui is connected to third-party APIs while handling local artifacts
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of open-webui’s mounted volume
Turn off persistent memory for the session
Use a local-only backend for open-webui
Review API-key handling before enabling tools
requires-engineering: segregate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: godot_rl_agents shows no write or network surfaces, while open-webui has broad network, browser, subprocess, and file access. There is no documented overlapping mutable resource between them, so direct write-write conflict is not evidenced; uncertainty stays low because the pair lacks a shared writable target in the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF open-webui is granted write access to artifacts produced by the game agent
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Avoid shared git working trees
Run open-webui without write access to the game repo
Use read-only mounts for imported artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can treat imported content, tool outputs, and memory as conversational context, so if godot_rl_agents outputs are fed into it, errors can propagate into downstream actions. The game agent is not documented as a verifier, and open-webui’s tool-use stack increases the chance of unverified outputs being acted on.
conditions: IF godot_rl_agents outputs are used as authoritative input to open-webui tools
IF open-webui is allowed to act on model-generated facts without human verification
mitigations: Require human approval before tool execution
Add a verification checklist for imported outputs
Disable autonomous actions in open-webui
Log and review any tool calls triggered by imported content
requires-engineering: add source-citation enforcement before actions

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, or regulated data classes are documented for godot_rl_agents, so compliance risk is mostly on open-webui’s side: it handles files, API keys, analytics, and can send data to third-party services. Because the pair does not show a specific regulated-data flow, this remains a low compliance concern.
conditions: IF regulated data is loaded into open-webui files, notes, or memory
IF open-webui is connected to external APIs without a DPA or residency review
mitigations: Do not load regulated data into open-webui
Disable analytics and external API connectors
Confirm retention settings before use
Use a local deployment for sensitive workflows
requires-engineering: document data-flow and residency boundaries
